content.text:
The campaign is finished and submitted, but no composition on this Mg–Sb–O line showed real photoactivity. I picked **index 0 (Sb fraction 0.085)** as best only because it had the highest reading, 0.00092% EQE, which is still at noise level.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.085 | 0.00092 |
| 4 | 0.126 | 0.00043 |
| 14 | 0.350 | 0.0 |
| 24 | 0.661 | -0.00014 |
| 29 | 0.807 | -0.00075 |

- **How I spent the budget:** I used all 5 EQE measurements, spread evenly across the line from Sb 0.08 to 0.81. I used none of the 5 XRD measurements and didn't run any phase or band-gap models.
- **What the results mean:** Every reading fell within ±0.001% of zero, including two slightly negative ones. The whole line looks inactive under 2.1 eV light at pH 1.4. That fits the known chemistry, though I didn't confirm it with the band-gap model: magnesium oxide and magnesium antimonates like MgSb₂O₆ are wide-gap insulators that can't absorb 2.1 eV photons.
- **Caveat:** The ranking is essentially noise. If a narrow active spot exists between my sample points, 5 measurements wouldn't have found it, but nothing in the data hints at one.
